name: Atom and molecule
description:
Atom: the smallest part of an element that still has the properties of that element.
Molecule: two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.

name: Common element symbols
description:
H: hydrogen
C: carbon
N: nitrogen
O: oxygen
Na: sodium
Cl: chlorine

name: Read a chemical formula
description: say which elements a chemical formula contains and how many atoms of each, for example that H₂O has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

name: Describe a chemical reaction
description: describe what happens in a chemical reaction, and explain why the number of atoms of each element is the same before and after.

name: Forms of energy
description:
Kinetic energy: energy something has because it moves.
Potential energy: energy stored because of position, such as water held behind a dam.
Chemical energy: energy stored in the bonds between atoms, such as in food and fuel.

name: Conservation of energy
description: Conservation of energy: energy is never used up or created, only converted from one form to another.

name: Units of energy and power
description:
J (joule): the unit of energy.
W (watt): one joule per second, the unit of power.
1 kWh: 3.6 million joules.

name: Describe an energy chain
description: describe the energy conversions from a power station to a lamp, and point out where energy is lost as heat.

name: Cell
description: Cell: the smallest unit that can be called alive. All living things are made of one or more cells.

name: Parts of the cell
description:
Nucleus: holds the DNA.
Mitochondrion: where cellular respiration releases energy.
Chloroplast: where photosynthesis happens, only in plant cells.
Cell wall: a stiff outer layer, only in plant cells.

name: Explain photosynthesis and respiration
description: explain how photosynthesis and cellular respiration are linked, using the words glucose, oxygen, carbon dioxide and energy.
